source.title: Stagewise Development in Neural Networks
source.authors: Jesse Hoogland; Liam Carroll; Daniel Murfet

record.file_problem: None; the full post text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: It examines induction-circuit formation and its timing relative to in-context learning using stagewise behavioral and geometric analyses, rather than reproducing the original method. The post describes small attention-only transformers modeled after Olsson et al.
record.gate_note: The post reports that previous-token scores start increasing in LM3, prefix scores increase in LM4, the induction circuit finishes forming in LM4, and the ICL score drops then. The LM2 relative n-gram loss result is not about the claim’s named induction or ICL behavior. The per-token-loss figure description gives no legible, separate result for the claimed training-loss bump.
record.test_reason: The post reports its own training-dynamics results on 3m-parameter 2-layer attention-only transformers modeled after Olsson et al. Using LLC and essential dynamics plus behavioral metrics, it times previous-token heads (LM3), prefix-score heads and circuit completion (LM4), and the ICL-score drop. This bears on V1, V2 and V7 with a different method aimed at the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that small language transformers develop in discrete, interpretable stages: bigrams, n-grams and positional information, starting previous-token heads, completing the induction circuit (coinciding with an ICL-score drop, i.e. better ICL), then converging. They also conclude that these stages can be found model- and data-agnostically via LLC and essential dynamics, often without being visible in the loss.
record.recipe_differences: The post studies small attention-only transformers modeled after Olsson et al., but uses local-learning-coefficient and essential-dynamics analyses alongside behavioral measures to identify developmental stages.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported induction-related developments occur at different stages: previous-token scores begin rising in LM3, while prefix scores and circuit completion occur in LM4.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear-regression transformers (50k parameters) acquire in-context regression in a discrete stage (LR2), followed by layer-norm and embedding collapse stages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context learning in non-language tasks also emerges in discrete, LLC-detectable developmental stages.

record.problems: Results in the post are qualitative; it gives no uncertainty estimates or controls for the induction-related measurements. The post does not report an explicit training-loss bump, and its per-token-loss figure description does not give a separate quantified result for that feature.
record.rows_left_out: The LM2 result about relative losses on representative 3- and 4-grams was left out because it does not directly measure induction behavior or the claimed ICL transition. The post's broad per-token-loss figure description supplies no separately attributable value for the claimed loss bump.

untested.parts: No direct test of K/Q-composition between the heads; no measure of copying [B] to the output; no ablation.
Abruptness or width of the window, and the bump in the loss curve, are not reported for the induction stage.
Whether LM3 and LM4 overlap or are fully separate transitions is not quantified.

missing.what: LLC-based stage boundaries. LM3 is a type B transition (LLC decreasing) and LM4 a type A transition, so the first induction sub-step shows LLC falling and completion shows it rising. Several stages are 'hidden from the loss'.
missing.locator: Figures 1 and 8; 'Interpreting the changes in LLC' section

missing.what: Essential dynamics finds a consistent cusp ('form') that, lifted to function space, corresponds to the induction mechanism AB...[A]B.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong summary of arXiv:2402.02364 (Hoogland et al. 2024), so it duplicates that paper and should be linked to it. All results are qualitative, with no uncertainty or controls. The ICL-score sign convention matters: 'drop' equals improved in-context learning.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not state that the heads explicitly copy the next token in the full [A][B] … [A] → [B] pattern, or report a direct composition intervention.
The post does not report an explicit training-loss bump or quantify the width or abruptness of the transition.
It studies small transformers, not large ones, and does not establish what fraction of large-model ICL is carried by induction heads.
No comparison across model families, sizes, training runs, other architectures, or modalities is reported.
The post does not vary data properties or training setup to test their effect on induction formation or persistent ICL.
It does not compare few-shot task learning with copying or test whether other mechanisms carry most few-shot learning.
The post identifies successive stages but does not resolve whether those stages are separate transitions or overlapping transitions.
